page.title: Latest news, sport and opinion from the Guardian

findings.title: h3 headings render at 5 different sizes
findings.evidence: “US midterm elections 2026 live Americans go to the” is 28px while “Full reportAmericans head to polls in midterm elec” is 14px (2×). Sizes seen: 14px ×12, 17px ×27, 20px ×62, 24px ×9, 28px ×6; weights: 400, 500. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h3 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Links to this page unfurl as a blank card
findings.evidence: No og:image. No og:title. Every share on iMessage, Discord, Slack, X and LinkedIn renders from these tags.
findings.fix: Add <meta property="og:image"> (1200×630), <meta property="og:title"> and <meta name="description"> with one specific sentence. In Next.js, export `metadata` from the page.

findings.title: Side-tab accent border (×2)
findings.evidence: “.dcr-1nw03rh::after — absolute 5px pseudo-element stripe (bottom: 0)” · “.dcr-1lb40gj::after — absolute 5px pseudo-element stripe (bottom: 0)”
findings.fix: Thick colored border on one side of a card — the most recognizable tell of AI-generated UIs. Use a subtler accent or remove it entirely.

findings.title: Above-the-fold is visually busy
findings.evidence: Quadtree decomposition of the first screen (text and photos masked out) needs 1300 leaves (calm pages run 50–250; busy ones 600+). Whitespace share 41%, text covers 17% of the viewport.
findings.fix: Remove one thing from the first screen. Reinecke's data says people rate low- and medium-complexity pages the same and punish high complexity; the gain is all in cutting, not adding.
findings.citation: Reinecke et al. CHI 2013; Tuch et al.: complexity drives the 50ms impression

findings.title: 2 marketing buzzwords
findings.evidence: “…sly watchable and effortlessly charming as a bli…” · “…e still see it as the future of cinema 6h ago Wha…”
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'

findings.title: No h1 on the page
findings.evidence: Screen readers and search engines use the h1 as the page's name.
findings.fix: Exactly one h1, saying what the page is.

findings.title: h2 is used at 2 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 20px ×16, 28px ×9. “US midterm elections 2026” is 28px, “In focus” is 20px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 20px ones are sub-sections, make them h3. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 10 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.

findings.title: Colourful first screen (M = 157, 5 hue bands)
findings.evidence: Colorfulness is the weaker of the two first-impression predictors, but many competing hues read as noise rather than brand.
findings.fix: One accent hue, one neutral ramp. Let photos or product shots carry the colour.

findings.title: Repeating-gradient stripes
findings.fix: Repeating-gradient stripes used as surface decoration are a recurring generated-UI signature. Reach for a deliberate texture or leave the surface plain.
